options.text: Avoid potassium-based salt substitutes and unnecessary potassium supplements
Take an extra potassium tablet with each dose of spironolactone
Increase bananas and salt substitutes freely because this drug wastes potassium
Stop checking laboratory potassium once therapy begins

items.stem: A client with heart failure starts spironolactone. Which teaching point is most important to prevent a serious electrolyte complication?

rationales.A: Correct. Spironolactone is potassium-sparing; OpenStax cautions against potassium salt substitutes and potassium-rich excess. Merck advises stopping potassium supplements and monitoring serum potassium because of hyperkalemia risk.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Adding potassium increases hyperkalemia risk with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Unlike loop/thiazide diuretics, potassium-sparing agents do not waste potassium; encouraging salt substitutes is unsafe teaching.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Merck: check potassium and creatinine regularly after starting or changing MRA dose.

items.stem: Complete the teaching plan for a client newly prescribed oral levothyroxine.

ngn.template: Take levothyroxine in the {B1} on an {B2}, at least {B3} before food. Separate doses from calcium or iron supplements by about {B4}.

B1.text: late evening with a large meal
middle of the night after a snack

B2.text: full stomach after a high-fiber meal
empty schedule with no timing guidance

rationales.B1a: Correct. OpenStax and DailyMed: take in the morning.
rationales.B1b: Incorrect. Evening with a large meal decreases absorption.
rationales.B1c: Incorrect. Caffeinated fluids can interfere with absorption.
rationales.B2a: Correct. Empty stomach improves absorption (OpenStax; DailyMed).
rationales.B2c: Incorrect. Bladder status is irrelevant to absorption teaching.
rationales.B2d: Incorrect. Timing relative to food matters.
rationales.B3a: Correct. At least one-half to one hour before food (OpenStax; DailyMed).
rationales.B3c: Incorrect. Excessively long and not the labeled interval.
rationales.B3d: Incorrect. Not a dosing interval for this teaching point.
rationales.B4a: Correct. Separate from calcium/iron by about 4 hours (OpenStax; DailyMed).

items.stem: A client takes combination cold remedies that contain acetaminophen plus as-needed acetaminophen tablets for pain. Which instruction is the priority safety teaching?

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: tally all sources; limit 4000 mg/24 h because of liver injury risk. Merck: acetaminophen poisoning causes hepatotoxicity; many OTC products contain APAP.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Combination products are a common hidden source of acetaminophen.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Overuse can cause serious hepatotoxicity.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Acetaminophen has a specific daily ceiling related to hepatotoxicity.

items.stem: An adult presents several hours after a large intentional acetaminophen overdose. Complete the bowtie.

conditions.text: Acetaminophen poisoning with risk of hepatotoxicity
Opioid overdose with pinpoint pupils alone
Simple foodborne gastroenteritis without toxin risk

actions.text: Obtain timed serum acetaminophen level and initiate N-acetylcysteine per protocol when indicated
Advise the client that no antidote exists and discharge immediately without evaluation
Support airway/circulation and escalate for hepatotoxicity monitoring as ordered
Give additional acetaminophen to “compete” with the overdose
Delay all care until liver failure is irreversible

parameters.text: Serial liver enzymes / clinical hepatotoxicity course
Response to N-acetylcysteine and ongoing mental status/vitals
Whether the client likes the hospital cafeteria menu
Single blood pressure only at triage with no reassessment

rationales.K1: Correct. Merck: acetaminophen poisoning risks hepatotoxicity; treat with N-acetylcysteine.
rationales.K2: Incorrect. Opioid overdose is a different toxidrome.
rationales.K3: Incorrect. Early GI symptoms may occur, but this is a toxic ingestion scenario.
rationales.K4: Incorrect. Hypoglycemia alone does not explain this ingestion history.
rationales.A1: Correct. Severity predicted by serum levels; NAC prevents/minimizes hepatotoxicity (Merck).
rationales.A2: Incorrect. An antidote (N-acetylcysteine) exists and early care matters.
rationales.A3: Correct. Supportive care and monitoring are required alongside antidote therapy.
rationales.P1: Correct. Hepatotoxicity evolves over 1–3 days; monitor liver injury course.
rationales.P2: Correct. Evaluate antidote response and clinical status.
rationales.P3: Incorrect. Not a clinical parameter for toxicity care.

items.stem: A hospitalized client has sudden vomiting and watery diarrhea consistent with norovirus gastroenteritis. Which infection-control action is most appropriate?

rationales.A: Correct. CDC norovirus guidance: Contact Precautions; gowns and gloves on entry. OpenStax supports PPE/gown-gloves for contact transmission risks.
rationales.B: Incorrect. CDC updated norovirus care to Contact + Standard, not Standard alone.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Routine Airborne isolation is not the norovirus recommendation.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Hand hygiene is essential; CDC promotes adherence during outbreaks.

rationales.C: Incorrect. Respirator is removed after leaving; gown/gloves are removed before exit.

options.text: Administer Rho(D) immune globulin as ordered within 72 hours of delivery
Withhold Rh immune globulin because it is never given after birth
Give Rh immune globulin only if the newborn is also Rh-negative
Delay Rh immune globulin until the next pregnancy begins

items.stem: An unsensitized Rh-negative postpartum client delivered an Rh-positive newborn 6 hours ago. Which action is the priority related to Rh sensitization prevention?

rationales.A: Correct. Merck postpartum care and OpenStax maternal-newborn: give Rho(D) immune globulin within 72 hours when an Rh-negative mother delivers an Rh-positive infant and is not sensitized.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Postpartum dosing is a key prevention step.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Postpartum dose is indicated when the newborn is Rh-positive (or type unknown per teaching), not when both are Rh-negative.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Waiting until the next pregnancy misses the postpartum prevention window.

items.stem: Which statement about the Apgar score is accurate?

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: describes condition at birth; does not determine individual prognosis; usually at 1 and 5 minutes. OpenStax: assessed at 1 and 5 minutes; does not predict neurologic outcome/mortality/morbidity for the neonate.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Merck: Apgar is not the tool that guides resuscitation; initial resuscitation steps occur before 1 minute.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Neither source treats Apgar as a lifelong prognosis guarantee.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Scoring is done right after birth at standard intervals.

items.stem: An adolescent with anorexia nervosa has rapid severe weight loss, symptomatic hypotension, and extreme bradycardia. Which action is the priority?

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: life-saving short-term intervention may be required for symptomatic hypotension, extreme bradycardia/arrhythmia, severe/rapid weight loss; consider hospitalization. OpenStax: hospitalization when medical monitoring is required; refeeding needs careful monitoring.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Extreme exercise and discharge with instability are unsafe.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Bradycardia, hypotension, and electrolyte complications are recognized.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Rapid unsupervised refeeding risks refeeding syndrome; medical monitoring is needed.
